title: OPCON Transition: Now It Is Time for the Commanders-in-Chief
gist: The author argues that the debate over wartime operational control (OPCON) transition from the US to South Korea is at the point of decision, noting the 2025 SCM agreement to verify FOC in 2026 and a 2026 US NDS that judges Korea able to lead deterrence of North Korea with limited US support. The excerpt is truncated.

insights.claim: At the 57th Security Consultative Meeting in 2025, South Korea and the US agreed to pursue verification of the full operational capability of the Future Combined Forces Command headquarters in 2026.
insights.speaker: Seol In-hyo
insights.so_what: The 2026 FOC verification is the near-term milestone for any OPCON handover.

insights.claim: The 2026 US National Defense Strategy assessed that South Korea can take primary responsibility for deterring North Korea with 'critical but more limited' US support.
insights.speaker: Seol In-hyo
insights.so_what: Signals reduced US force commitment on the peninsula, relevant for Korea defense spending.

insights.claim: The author contends that more than 20 years since formalizing OPCON transition and over a decade of conditions-based preparation, a mature South Korea justifies deciding now, framing it as a decision for the two commanders-in-chief.
insights.speaker: Seol In-hyo
insights.so_what: Raises odds of an announced OPCON timeline under the Lee administration.
